items.title: Jim H. Dunbar Jr. Interview, 1959-11-28
items.q: I think one of the guys had played with Ray Charles, for example.

ctx.x: band names. It doesn't have to be specific.

Well, the one that comes to my mind soonest, or first, is, uh, Young Tuxedos. Uh, see, not one reason for that is I've heard them more, but, um, I've heard several of the other groups. Uh, of course, being, uh, you know, Yankee and from up north and never having a really, you know, heard any records of these groups. Being able to see them and watch, perhaps watch a parade or a funeral or something, is it, if, if, if, if it's nothing else, it's, uh, unique is a overused word. I've been using it too much, but it's…

Well, you know, the thing that really gets me about that band, it's a brass band and the other brass bands have air monitors. But it's like Danny Ruffer said about it. If somebody ever recorded that barrel house brass band and it is really barrel house. Now they can sit there and read those directors and play them pretty straight. You know, you've heard that, about it. No deal. Mm-hmm. But God, they can't really get down to the line, you know. See, it's exciting. Yeah.
